analysis.title: Goldman's Favorite Trade If Democrats Sweep The Midterms
key_insights: Prediction markets have priced a Democratic sweep over the past month, while the stocks that should benefit most have fallen over the past three weeks. Polymarket and Kalshi have Democrats above 90% to take the House and a full sweep at about 70%. Kalshi's sweep odds are 68%.
Goldman's Louis Miller says the market trades two things, AI and oil, and that demand for AI- and oil-uncorrelated trades has never been higher. His main answer is Healthcare.

Goldman's S&P ex-AI index (SPXXAI) worked 'perfectly in October'. On Thursday it posted its third-best day of outperformance vs the S&P ever (+2.2pp) and is about 5 points ahead of the index over the past year. Miller cautions that a weaker growth outlook warrants special caution on pockets that benefited mainly from a short squeeze.

Sweep trade: Goldman's favorite long is the Affordable Care Act Beneficiaries basket (GSHLCACA). Reauthorizing the enhanced ACA premium tax credits, which expired at end-2025, should improve earnings for hospitals, outpatient providers and health insurers facing rising bad debt and uncompensated care costs. Goldman calls the entry point attractive. The basket is down roughly 7% relative to the S&P ex-AI from its early-October peak while sweep odds kept rising.

Other midterm calls: AI Power (GSENEPOW) gets a tailwind if more power supply is sold as the cure for electricity inflation. AI hardware ex-Power (GSTMTAIH) could suffer if policymakers make datacenters bear more grid cost, which could weaken datacenter project economics.

Corporate tax basket (GSPUTAXP) is 'worth putting on your radar'. Because of the presidential veto, midterms are unlikely to change tax law and 2027-28 earnings are largely insulated, but a higher rate is a risk beyond 2029.

Zero Hedge's critique: the veto that protects corporate tax rates also blocks an ACA subsidy bill. Trump has promised to 'veto everything' a Democratic Congress sends him and let the credits expire. The realistic route is a shutdown or debt ceiling standoff, where per Citi the price of Democratic votes may be delaying spending cuts rather than adding subsidies. The 7% slide may be the market pricing the veto.

Goldman's revamped Healthcare AI Beneficiaries basket (GSHLCAIP) now covers diagnostics, genomic and biological data, laboratory automation and precision medicine. It is up about 38% YTD vs roughly 17% for Goldman's broad AI basket and 20% for the S&P Health Care sector. Miller says it has low correlation to AI, rates and oil.
Goldman credit strategist Amanda Lynam named Healthcare/Pharma among the IG sectors with the lowest correlation to AI spreads, the new 'defensives'.
Goldman's systematic team pitches the Growth Value Rotator, up 27% YTD long-only (GSRHBUBG) and 18% long/short (GSRHBUBT), as a way to trade growth/value swings without calling timing or direction.

Goldman's Software vs. Semis pair (GSPUSOSE) is up 88% from June lows, with a 3x beta to the momentum unwind. Miller says the AI-disruption narrative for software is 'a lot more nuanced than a year ago'. Software forward P/E rose from 17x to 23x in four months, so earnings must separate companies with structural earnings pressure from those with competitive moats. Momentum has been 'unplayable' for weeks.

Miller's 'food for thought': the Binance hack (about $6.3 billion, described as the biggest heist in crypto history) points to underpriced AI disruption in insurance. The sector benefited from a defensive rally in October but could face significant earnings headwinds from underappreciated underwriting risk (citing a Munich Re white paper), particularly if risk relief rotates Financials flows back to banks.
Goldman expects the cybersecurity TAM to keep growing as AI use cases spread and notes rising client interest in non-US ways to play it.

European banks posted their worst month since March 2023. Goldman does not expect significant OAT-Bund tightening near-term but thinks the selloff looks overdone given limited spillover risk and solid fundamentals, with ROTE seen expanding 200bp through 2028. Preferred expression is Greek banks (GSXEGRBK), which de-rated about 10% in sympathy and are separating on solid Q3 NII beats, an Alpha Bank capital markets day on Nov 5 and MSCI's developed-market upgrade in May 2027.

Japan banks have 'disconnected from solid underlying earnings'. Goldman thinks BoJ signaling for a December hike (Ueda left the door open Friday, one board member already voted to hike) sets up a year-end relief rally. Risk: an 'escalate to de-escalate' strategy with Iran does not materialize, driving incremental inflation and rates pain.

European Defense basket (GSSBDEFE) is up 13% in three weeks, partly from non-AI exposure and high short crowding. GS research expects European defense spending to grow at an 8% CAGR over FY25-30 while valuations imply declining medium-term earnings. The desk sees potential for a roughly 30% re-rating back to September 2025 levels if Q3 results show production ramps and cash generation on track.

Zero Hedge view: Healthcare AI's low correlation is real and insurers look complacent on cyber risk, but the headline sweep trade is questionable. With a Fed that is still hiking, Brent above $110 and Washington reportedly preparing Gulf allies for operations against Iran after the vote, gridlock is the most likely outcome.
